patch_description:
This redesign uses a flattened graph architecture instead of coordinate-heavy global structures. It precomputes all-pairs shortest-path first moves in compact arrays, represents routes as strings plus flattened cell IDs, and evaluates dirtiness in one linear scan using first/last visit timestamps and gap accumulation rather than per-cell visit vectors.

The search is organized around a compact simulated-annealing engine with modular mutation operators: local detours, cancellation, shortest-path compression, path reversal, targeted high-dirt revisits, and targeted segment replacement. Several weighted randomized DFS tours are evaluated before optimization to provide a better initial state. This substantially reduces allocation overhead and route-evaluation cost, allowing more meaningful search iterations within the time limit.
